newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan to promote bonds to Asia banks.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan to promote bonds to Asia banks.

text.p: Saskatchewan Finance Minister Janice MacKinnon said on Thursday she planned to promote her province's bonds to Asian bankers on a 10-day trip to Hong Kong and Japan.

"We feel it is important to get out the message about Saskatchewan's impressive fiscal turnaround and growing economy to help attract new investment and business opportunities," MacKinnon said in a statement.
Saskatchewan presented its fourth consecutive balanced budget on March 20 when it projected a C$24.1 million surplus in fiscal 1997/98 (April/March).
Saskatchewan is a major agricultural and potash exporter.

MacKinnon, who flies to Asia on Friday, is scheduled to meet with officials from the Bank of China, Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi, Industrial Bank of Japan, Meiji Life and Nippon Life as well as with Canadian banks and investment dealers in Asia.
MacKinnon also plans to meet with Kampo, the Japanese post-office bureau, which is one of the world's largest investors, the statement said.
